title: Give the freight board one deadline for every carrier

blocks.text: A freight marketplace shows shippers a board of quotes from every carrier it works with. The product team promised the board within two seconds, whatever the carriers do: a carrier that has not answered by then is shown as too late, and one whose API fails is shown without a quote. The first version waited for every carrier, so one carrier with a stuck API kept the board from ever appearing.

items: `collect(...)`: ask every carrier on the pool and build the board's lines.

blocks.text: When you're done, the board comes by its deadline with one line per carrier, in the carriers' order, and a carrier that missed the deadline is shown as `too late` and stops using a pool thread. About twelve lines in total.
The tests ask carriers on a real `ExecutorService`; some of them never answer until the test ends.

cases.says: every carrier's quote, or the note that its call failed, appears in the carriers' order
the board is built by its deadline even when a carrier never answers, and shows that carrier as too late
a late carrier keeps its place on the board as too late, and the carriers after it are still shown
a carrier still being asked when the deadline comes is interrupted, so its thread goes back to the pool

origin.section: invokeAll's Deadline Cancels the Stragglers, and Their get() Throws an Unchecked CancellationException

concepts: get() on a cancelled future throws CancellationException, which is unchecked, so a loop that handles only ExecutionException ends at the first late task.
A timed invokeAll returns by its deadline with a future for every task in order, and cancels with an interrupt the tasks still running.
